speaker: fitz
text:
Airplane windows have rounded corners. Square ones would show more sky, so why not?
Every flight, the cabin is pressurized and the metal stretches, then relaxes when you land.
A sharp corner piles that stretch into one tiny spot. After thousands of flights, cracks start there.
In 1954, the Comet, the first jet airliner, broke apart from cracks like that.
Round corners spread the stretch out. No single weak spot.
